Title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

Authors: Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li, Siyuan Zhuang, Ying Sheng, Lianmin Zheng
Abstract: High throughput serving of large language models requires batching enough requests together to fully utilize the hardware, but existing systems struggle because the key-value cache for each request is large and grows dynamically. Memory is wasted by fragmentation and by duplication across parallel samples. This work observes that the inefficiency comes from how the cache is stored, not from the size of the model itself, and proposes an attention algorithm inspired by operating system virtual memory paging. The algorithm allows cache blocks to be stored non-contiguously, so nearly all of the reserved memory can be used for actual tokens instead of padding. A serving system built around this idea reaches substantially higher throughput than strong baselines on the same hardware and latency target, and the gain is largest when sequences are long and output lengths are variable. The implementation is released as an open source project and has been adopted by several production deployments.
Comments:Accepted at SOSP 2023
Subjects:Computation and Language (cs.CL)
